text:
Very impressed how seamless the integration between this app and the apple health/fitness infrastructure, including my watch has been.
I’ve been able to record all workout, walks etc simply by using my watch
With the workout routines I really like the structured way it starts, builds then cools down.
A couple of suggestions, 
On the work out apps have more routines and allow user to pick which ones they want to do on a particular day or build a series of workouts. For instance when I started to use this app there was a workout called leg strength which was excellent, but has now been superseded by another lower body routine which is no where near as challenging. Could we have more routines in the Strength Intro series, 
On those workouts for the times exercises (eg greatest stretch) have a beep to indicate start, half way and finish with a 5 second period between each to get ready. It’s not always possible to keep the screen in view (eg dead bug) when performing the exercise.
Allow the user to insert their own exercises from your DB of possibles, I know its easy to pause the routine do your  your own and then carry on but then there is no trail of progress.

A couple of minor criticisms
In my profile it asks my primary sport and only offers running or cycling, I’ve never done either of these and am never likely to. My goal is general fitness commensurate with my age range. Either add other groups or allow a ‘none of the above’ option
In training plans under general training it points my to Runna, As pointed out above I’m never going to start running so why wouldn’t general training point me to workout routines or an appropriate partner ?
Other than that great app and worth the subscription.

text:
I was hanging out with my friend one day when she told me about this app, it looked like a useful tool to navigate my city for walking/biking so I decided to download it. Upon downloading, there was a pop up advertising their subscription plans. The options were weekly, monthly or annual but they also offered a month long free trial. I went with that just to get a feel of the app and if I’d really use it. 

After I clicked on free trial, I was asked to make a payment of $0.00 and on the very bottom it stated I would be charged by the end of this month. I “paid” them only to get a call from my bank less than 20 minutes later asking if the recent $85.59 charge was fraud. I wasn’t even aware Strava was trying to charge me so I told them to dispute it. I deleted my newly made account along with the app because it didn’t seem like a trustworthy platform, trying to charge me for an annual subscription when I simply wanted a free trial. 

I thought the issue was resolved until I tried to download a different app about a day later, and since there was a “pending charge” for Strava, there was some sort of lock on my account. I called Apple and they told me since I disputed it with my bank I’d have to pay the $85.59 and then request a refund. That seemed a little strange to me but I went ahead and did so. 

I’ve now requested a refund through Apple 2x and each time it’s been denied. I’ve reached out to Strava and it seems I keep getting automated responses that are no help. So now, I’m out $85.59 and I don’t even have anything to show for it since I deleted my account completely. 

I have never been scammed like this. I’m not sure how, but the Apple support assistant told me they could tell I only had the account for less than 2-3 hours and I did select free trial…but they charged me for a year long subscription. 

In my opinion, this app isn’t worth it. I feel so embarrassed and upset. If I had known in hindsight all of this would happen, I simply would’ve looked up a map of my city and circled the trails/paths I’d like to check out instead of going through all of this to get my money back.
title: Be aware of the “free trial” !

text:
I ride with a cycling club. The most attractive feature offered by Strava to our club members is the Club Leader Board.  But it only considers the current week.  Members have requested that the board be expanded to also include periods such as:
(1) Current month
(2) Current quarter
(3) Current year.
The response they received from Strava is “write a proposal for our proposal page.”  This strikes us as an effective means of deep sixing the idea, since, according to our survey, over 99% of Strava users don’t even know there is such a page.  It is self-evident that if Clubs appreciate Leader Boards on a weekly basis, they will love Leader Boards on a monthly, quarterly, and yearly basis even more.  Please get off your hands and provide this benefit which Clubs are yearning for!

text:
I have been a paid Strava subscriber for more than six years, one of the main reasons I subscribed was the excellent annual “Year in Sport” report. It provides a meaningful summary of my activities and progress, and it is something I have always looked forward to each January. This year I never received a notification that my 2025 report was available, so I missed the opportunity to view it. I was extremely disappointed to discover that the report is only available until around 23rd January and is then removed completely.

For me, this feature is more than just an interesting summary. After recovering from a major accident, my Strava records have been an important way of tracking both my initial disability and my gradual improvement over time. The Year in Sport report provides a unique and motivating record of that journey, and losing access to it is particularly frustrating.

Removing the report after only a few weeks makes little sense for a paid service. A yearly summary should remain available for at least 12 months - ideally permanently within a subscriber’s profile.

Because of this policy, I have now cancelled by Strava subscription. I hope Strava will reconsider and make a Year in Sport reports permanently accessible in the future. After all, isn’t Strava all about well earned personal fitness statistics?
title: Annual “Year in Sport” Report Removed Too Soon - Subscription Cancelled

text:
I first joined Strava over 10 years, back when it was the niche platform of choice for cycling/running/triathloning weirdos like myself. Why would I use any other social media when there was one dedicated to sport? It was amazing.

I understood why the subscription fees came in during COVID - it exploded in popularity, and had to cover the running costs incurred by the millions of new people signing up. However, recently, more and more features (many of which are very basic) have been creeping behind the paywall, and it’s now reaching a point where the free version is almost unusable. This is extremely sad, especially as many of these changes can no longer be justified, and it’s simply a way of forcing people to pay for their existing data.

So after more than a decade, I’m going to be waving goodbye to Strava. Thanks for all the good times down the years - hopefully you’ll recognise one day that this current money-grabbing approach is not the answer to long-term success.
